body: NASA/Clayton Rougelot On Aug. 24, technicians at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida began installing the four RS‑25 engines in the core stage of the agency’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket that will carry the Artemis III crew into low Earth orbit in 2027. Each RS‑25 engine has a unique serial number that records its detailed flight history. The four engines assigned to Artemis III — E2054, E2057, E2048, and E2052 — previously powered multiple space shuttle missions. Engine 2048 helped launch NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik’s earlier mission aboard space shuttle Atlantis during STS‑129. It also flew on Space Shuttle Discovery during STS‑95 in 1998, the mission that returned 77-year‑old space pioneer U.S. Sen. John Glenn to orbit, making him the oldest person to fly in space at that time.

title: Pixel 11’s big modem switch hasn’t ended familiar connectivity complaints
summary: Early owners report Wi-Fi, 5G and Bluetooth problems.
body: TL;DR Some Pixel 11 owners are reporting connectivity problems, including unreliable 5G/mobile data, Wi-Fi dropouts, and Bluetooth issues. The reports are limited to a small number of users, with plenty of Pixel 11 owners saying their connectivity is working perfectly. It’s too early to blame the new MediaTek modem, as carriers, network conditions, routers, firmware, and individual hardware could all be factors. Google’s switch from Samsung Exynos to a MediaTek modem on the Pixel 11 series was supposed to close one of the longest-running chapters in Pixel history. After years of complaints around reception, connectivity, and cellular battery drain, the new modem arrived as one of the generation’s most meaningful upgrades. But just weeks after the Pixel 11 series went on sale, some owners are reporting connectivity problems that sound uncomfortably familiar. Reports across Reddit include phones showing a 5G icon with no internet access, refusing to connect to Wi-Fi, dropping Wi-Fi performance, and struggling to maintain a cellular connection.

The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra (SM-X940) has appeared on Geekbench 7 with 2,760 points in single-core and 9,291 in multi-core (spotted via GSMArena ) . title: Google finds another way to push Search users to AI Mode
summary: AI Overviews are automatically expanding for some searches.
body: TL;DR Some Google Search queries are returning fully expanded AI Overview summaries. These expanded summaries include a text box labeled Ask anything that links to AI Mode. It seems this is only the case on desktop. Google’s been working at making AI Mode a more prominent part of Search for some time. Now, it’s taken another step to that end: some AI Overview summaries are now showing up fully expanded, complete with a text box where you can type follow-up questions that’ll launch an AI Mode interaction. Previously, these text boxes only appeared when you clicked Show more at the bottom of an AI Overview. This change hasn’t been officially announced, but was recently pointed by co-founder of SEO agency Nectiv Chris Long on X (via WinFuture ). Today, certain search terms return results that begin with an expanded AI Overview answer that takes up quite a bit of space, along with a box labeled Ask anything, inviting users to stay inside Google’s ecosystem rather than scrolling down to the websites it’s pulling information from.

title: Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 fixes a long-standing APK sideloading pain point
summary: Google introduces a new inline dialog box and one-time install permissions to make installing unknown apps safer and easier.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 improves the process of granting apps permission to install other apps with a new inline dialog, eliminating the need to leave the active app. The update also adds one-time install permissions that are automatically revoked once the APK has finished installing. Users retain the ability to grant apps permanent permissions to install other apps. Google released Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 last week, bringing new additions such as a dedicated Agent Dashboard . However, the update also tackles a long-standing security and convenience pain point by introducing one-time installation permissions for unknown apps, making APK sideloading significantly safer without compromising convenience for power users. On older Android versions, sideloading an APK outside official app stores requires granting the host app (such as a browser or a file manager) the “Install unknown apps” permission.

title: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude quietly get worse over time. This hidden setting fixes them
summary: Your favorite AI chatbot might be remembering a little too much.
body: I’ve been using LLM-based AI in some capacity for roughly half a decade, and in that time, the industry has changed significantly. Not only have newer competitors like Gemini and Claude arrived on the scene, but older tools like ChatGPT have also evolved dramatically. We’ve seen better third-party app integration, increased reasoning capabilities, and countless other advancements. However, I would argue that the ability to retain memories matters most. Retaining context from previous conversations helps the AI better anticipate your needs within a single session. It also allows the tool to learn more about you, ensuring that future conversations are tailored to your preferences. However, there is a real downside to memory accumulation that not everyone considers. I’ve found that starting with a new AI usually requires significant input to generate the responses I need and fully understand my user profile. Once it reaches this data “sweet spot,” the AI becomes much more pleasant to use. Yet, slowly over time, the experience often seems to degrade again.
